# HatchZip

> HatchZip extracts ZIP, 7z, tar, .tar.gz, RAR and split archives in place: it extracts from the end of the archive and cuts each finished part off the archive file (a .tar.gz from the front, freeing the compressed bytes already used), so it needs free space for the extracted files only, not for the files and the archive together. Free and open source (MIT OR Apache-2.0), for Windows, macOS and Linux. Command line `hatchzip` (short name `hz`) and a desktop app.

The archive is used up as it extracts: when the run finishes, only the extracted files are left. It checks that the extraction fits before it changes anything, and an interrupted run resumes when the same command is run again.

## Install

- Linux and macOS: `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xevrion/hatchzip/main/install.sh | sh` (installs `hatchzip` and `hz` for the current user, no root; checks SHA-256)
- Windows (PowerShell): `irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xevrion/hatchzip/main/install.ps1 | iex`
- With Rust: `cargo install hatchzip` (without RAR support; `--features rar` adds it, which compiles UnRAR's C++ source under its own license). Every download above includes RAR support
- Desktop app: [Windows setup](https://github.com/xevrion/hatchzip/releases/latest/download/HatchZip-x64-setup.exe), [Windows MSI](https://github.com/xevrion/hatchzip/releases/latest/download/HatchZip-x64.msi) (same install as the setup, for deployment tools; install one or the other),[macOS Apple Silicon](https://github.com/xevrion/hatchzip/releases/latest/download/HatchZip-aarch64.dmg), [macOS Intel](https://github.com/xevrion/hatchzip/releases/latest/download/HatchZip-x86_64.dmg), [Linux AppImage](https://github.com/xevrion/hatchzip/releases/latest/download/HatchZip-x86_64.AppImage), [.deb](https://github.com/xevrion/hatchzip/releases/latest/download/hatchzip_amd64.deb), [.rpm](https://github.com/xevrion/hatchzip/releases/latest/download/hatchzip-x86_64.rpm)

## Use

- `hatchzip check game.zip`: shows whether it fits, changes nothing (exit 3 if it doesn't fit)
- `hatchzip extract game.zip -y`: extracts into `game/` next to the archive and removes the archive as it goes; `-y` skips the confirmation for unattended use
- `hatchzip extract game.zip -o DIR`: extract somewhere else
- `hatchzip extract game.zip --verify-first`: read everything once before deleting anything
- `hatchzip extract game.zip --keep-archive`: a normal extraction that keeps the archive unchanged; needs space for all extracted files, and `check --keep-archive` shows whether it fits. Resumes like any other run and keeps keeping the archive. In the desktop app: clear "Remove the archive during extraction"; in the right-click menu: "Extract here (keep archive)"
- `hatchzip extract a.zip b.7z c.tar.gz`: several archives one after another, each checked for space just before it starts; the first that does not complete stops the run, with a summary, and sets the exit code. `check`, `test` and `list` also take several archives
- `hatchzip restore game.zip`: turn a half-extracted archive back into a normal archive
- `hatchzip list game.zip`, `hatchzip test game.zip`: list or verify without changing anything
- Passwords: `--password` or the `HATCHZIP_PASSWORD` environment variable
- Exit codes: 0 done, 1 error, 2 usage, 3 not enough space, 4 damaged archive, 5 password needed or wrong, 130 stopped (run again to resume). With several archives, the code of the first one that did not succeed

## Limits

- A 7z made with 7-Zip's default settings is one solid block; it needs free space for that whole block, and `check` says so first.
- A `.tar.gz` frees space while it extracts only on filesystems that can free part of a file (NTFS, APFS, ext4, XFS, btrfs). On FAT32 and exFAT it needs room for the archive and the files at once, and `check` says so.
- `.tar.xz` and `.tar.zst` are not supported yet.
- RAR (RAR 5 and RAR 4, single files and `.part1.rar` or `.rar`/`.r00` volume sets) is freed file by file, each volume deleted once empty. A solid RAR is extracted only with `--keep-archive`; RAR archives with encrypted file names or links are refused before anything changes.

## Safety

- No network access: no networking code or library, no telemetry, no update checks. CI fails if an HTTP, TLS or socket library enters the dependencies.
- Not code-signed yet, so Windows SmartScreen and a few machine-learning antivirus engines can flag the downloads. Each release file has a `.sha256` checksum and signed build provenance (`gh attestation verify <file> --repo xevrion/hatchzip`); see [Verify your download](https://hatchzip.dev/verify.html).
